sources.title: Request for SEARs: proposed construction and operation of data centre, 3-4 Apollo Place and 87-91 Mars Road, Lane Cove West (Mars Road Data Centre), 6 March 2026
sources.publisher: Willowtree Planning (NSW) Pty Ltd (filed with and published by the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure)
sources.attribution: Willowtree Planning (NSW) Pty Ltd, via the NSW Planning Portal
sources.summary: The consultant's SEARs request (letter dated 6 March 2026, ref WTJ25-464; 36 pages) seeks SEARs under the Rapid Assessment Framework for a State significant development application for a new data centre 'to be known as the Mars Road Data Centre' on Lot 8 DP241877 (3 Apollo Place, 3,473.3 m2), Lot 9 DP241877 (4 Apollo Place, 1,289.5 m2), Lot 100 DP622160 (87 Mars Road, 2,428.2 m2) and Lot 1 DP732557 (91 Mars Road, 7,852.9 m2), plus part of Lot 1 DP1271404 (1 Sirius Road, which holds the Lane Cove West Data Centre SSD-9741 and Apollo Place Data Centre SSD-67407231 approvals). It proposes demolition, consolidation of the four lots, and a five-storey data centre with roof plant, about 13,800 m2 GFA, 37.4 m high, total IT load about 140 MW, about 120 back-up generators, diesel and lithium-battery storage and two driveways (site about 15,044 m2). It states that 1 Sirius Road will not form part of the site when the EIS is lodged (boundary adjustment and consolidation into a single lot) and that 'Future development proposed on the Site will operate independently to both the Lane Cove West and Apollo Place Data Centres.' The proponent table names only the planning consultant; no developer or operator is identified.

sources.title: CDC Investor Day Presentation (Infratil Investor Update, 16 September 2026)
sources.publisher: CDC Data Centres (presentation released by Infratil Limited, NZX/ASX: IFT)
sources.summary: CDC's 32-slide investor day deck, released by Infratil on 16 September 2026 with its 'Data centre demand drives growth and guidance increase' announcement. Slide 8 ('Operating capacity has more than doubled over the last 18 months') states that 'CDC has delivered seven large-scale data centres since FY25, all of which are now contributing meaningfully to CDC's earnings generation' and labels them Melbourne Brooklyn 2, Sydney Eastern Creek 5 & 6, Sydney Marsden Park 1, Canberra Hume 6, Canberra Beard 1 and Auckland Hobsonville 2. Slide 6 maps each campus's data centres with a legend of operational, under construction and future development: Eastern Creek EC1-EC6 are shown operational. Slide 9 says construction is progressing at Laverton (first building expected operational in late FY27), Marsden Park (multiple data centres across FY28-29) and Perth Maddington (structure of the inaugural Perth data centre nearing completion). CDC reports 350 MW of deployed capacity generating revenue (as at 31 August 2026).

sources.title: Spotsylvania County Planning Commission: agenda packet for the meeting of 16 September 2026 (Crossroads Technology Campus 2232 review and SUP26-0003 staff report, applicant narrative and attachments)
sources.summary: Executive summaries and staff report for '(VOTE ONLY) Crossroads Technology Campus 2232 Comprehensive Plan Review' and 'SUP26-0003: "Crossroads Technology Campus" RCK DIGITAL CROSSROADS LLC'. The applicant requests a special use permit for a data center campus of up to 2,087,000 square feet of data center buildings with three electrical substations on about 555 acres, tax parcels 37-A-20 (3215 Eagle Drive), 37-A-21 and 37-A-17D, on the north side of Eagle Drive (Route 736), Lee Hill School Drive (Route 635) and Mills Drive (Route 17), adjacent on the west to the CSX railroad; the land is currently vacant and forested; the Generalized Development Plan (Kimley-Horn, 26 August 2026) shows seven data center buildings (no more than 75 feet, two-storey configuration), three substations, utility buildings and water tanks, with about 192 acres disturbed. Staff recommend approval with conditions; the proposed conditions tie the Facility to parcels 37-A-20, 37-A-21 and 37-A-17D. Staff note that one transmission option would extend a line from near the PowerHouse 95 site along Route 17. The attached Rappahannock Electric Cooperative High Energy Use Facility form (submitted 7 August 2026) gives the applicant's estimated electric load as 894 MW, to be served by three new 230/34.5 kV 298 MVA distribution substations, with Dominion Energy as transmission provider; REC notes the load is the applicant's unverified estimate.
sources.date_semantics: Packet for the meeting of 16 September 2026, published on the county CivicClerk portal on 16 September 2026 (publishOn 2026-09-16T15:23Z). Project identity, parcel and scope context; the requests were pending on that date. The 894 MW figure is the applicant's requested electric load reported by the utility, not IT capacity.

sources.summary: The county's Pending Planning Cases layer lists two Gardner Property cases in the Brentsville Magisterial District: special use permit SUP2027-00008, transmittal date 24 September 2026, status Under Review, and rezoning REZ2023-00018, transmittal date 22 March 2023, status Under Review. The SUP is a request to allow data centers and an electric substation outside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District, with development waivers and modifications including building height up to 66 feet (rooftop mechanical equipment and screening walls up to a further 15 feet, at most 81 feet in total) and a floor area ratio up to 0.56. The rezoning would change about 82.74 acres from A-1, Agricultural, and B-1, General Business, to PBD, Planned Business District, with an M-2 land bay, to allow data center buildings and an electric substation. The project area lies north and north-west of the intersections of Gardner Manor Place, McGraws Corner Drive and Nolan Road, mostly east of the North Fork stream and west of the railroad. Both cases carry the same polygon (82.56 geodesic acres; the county's GIS acreage is 82.57).
sources.date_semantics: The status observation is the TransmittalDate of SUP2027-00008 (2026-09-24T04:00Z, midnight Eastern daylight time on 24 September 2026): the date on which the planning office accepted and transmitted the special use permit application for data centers. It is not a decision; no approval, permit or physical work is asserted. The layer carries no record-version timestamp; published_at is the capture date (26 October 2026), the date on which this record version was observed being served by the county.
sources.personal_data_note: Query omits the case-planner, email and phone fields; owner fields were not requested anywhere. No personal names are recorded.

sources.title: Prince William County Pending Planning Cases layer definition (CountyMapper Land Development layer 2)
sources.summary: The layer 'represents the active cases in process in the Planning Office', including rezonings, special use permits, comprehensive plan amendments and proffer amendments; the cases 'have been accepted by the Current Planning Division and are in process to be heard by the Planning Commission and/or the Board of County Supervisors', and remain on the layer until approval or denial by the Board or withdrawal by the applicant. Date fields are referenced to Eastern time with daylight saving.
sources.date_semantics: Undated layer description; used to interpret TransmittalDate and the later-status review (a case still listed has not been decided or withdrawn).

sources.summary: All 134 active planning cases. Data-centre cases transmitted on or after 2 August 2026 are Madera Farm SUP2027-00002 (19 August, Pending) and Gardner Property SUP2027-00008 (24 September, Under Review). Other pending data-centre cases (for example Six Towers Industrial Park, Manassas Corporate Center 8, Atlantic Funding Development, Southgate South, Project Industry and University Business Park) were transmitted before the window. The three Digital Gateway rezonings are listed as void under the 29 July 2026 Court of Appeals order.

sources.title: Prince William County Data Center Campuses layer (78 campus polygons, captured 26 October 2026)
sources.summary: The county campus layer contains 78 data-center campus polygons. It lists Gardner Property (REZ2023-00018) as a Pending campus in a proposed PBD district, 82.57 GIS acres and 2,017,100 sq ft planned gross floor area, outside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay (DCOOD 'No'), with a polygon identical to the SUP2027-00008 case polygon. The nearest other campus polygons are Amazon Village Place Technology Park (REZ2020-00024, Planned; 18 m from the Gardner polygon) and NTT Grove at Gainesville (REZ2021-00001, Planned; 334 m). Madera Farm has no campus polygon; the nearest campus polygon to it, Stack Infrastructure NVA02 YFT, is 6.3 km away.
sources.date_semantics: Undated planning geometry; LastEditDate values (25 September 2026 for these records) are administrative edits. Identity and distinctness context only; planned gross floor area is a planning figure, not capacity.
